note: The creative catalog. The board shows these as pickers; the engine reads the same keys. Add or tweak entries here and both follow.

C.name: Cool with a punch
C.style: Mostly cool, nonchalant and confident, like telling a friend a wild fact without trying too hard, then a quick, sharp punch of energy on the big reveal lines before settling back. Engaging and fun, never over the top. Around 165 to 175 words a minute.

A.name: Calm and deadpan
A.style: Calm, matter-of-fact, slightly deadpan narrator. Quick but unhurried, even energy, never hyped. Let the facts be the surprise. Tiny pauses before reveals, a dry hint of a smirk. Around 165 to 175 words a minute.

B.name: Punchy host
B.style: Bright, punchy, fast Shorts host. Every sentence lands with crisp emphasis and rising energy into each reveal, but it stays conversational, never shouting. Quick breaths, almost no dead air. Around 175 to 185 words a minute.

story.name: Campfire storyteller
story.style: A warm, intimate storyteller leaning in at a campfire. Unhurried, vivid, savouring the details, voice drops low for the strange parts and lifts with wonder at the turn. Natural breaths, real pauses, never reading. Around 150 to 160 words a minute.

doc.name: Documentary gravitas
doc.style: A grounded nature-documentary narrator with gravitas. Low, resonant, measured, every line weighted. Lets silence sit after big facts. Awe without melodrama. Around 140 to 150 words a minute.

trailer.name: Movie trailer hype
trailer.style: Epic movie-trailer narrator building a hero moment. Starts low and restrained, tension climbing line by line, then a big confident lift on the payoff line. Short punchy phrases, dramatic pauses before the drop. Powerful but never shouting. Around 140 to 160 words a minute.

anime.name: Anime narrator
anime.style: Energetic anime-opening narrator. Bright, intense, earnest, every stake feels life or death, sharp emphasis on power words, a breathless rush into the climax and a proud, determined final line. Around 170 to 185 words a minute.

sports.name: Play-by-play commentator
sports.style: A live sports commentator calling the moment as it happens. Fast, rising excitement, quick reactions, disbelief on the big play, then a satisfied wrap. Around 180 to 195 words a minute.

survival.name: Urgent survival guide
survival.style: Calm under pressure, like a survival instructor talking you through a disaster in real time. Low, steady, urgent, clipped sentences, every instruction matters. Tension rises, never panic. Around 160 to 170 words a minute.

eerie.name: Eerie whisper
eerie.style: Hushed, close-mic, unsettling late-night mystery voice. Slow, deliberate, half-whispered, lingering on strange details, a chill in the pauses. Never cheesy. Around 130 to 145 words a minute.

noir.name: Hard-boiled noir
noir.style: A 1940s hard-boiled detective narrating his case. Dry, gravelly, world-weary, cynical one-liners, slow drawl with sharp snaps on the punchlines. Around 140 to 155 words a minute.

radio.name: Late-night radio theorist
radio.style: A late-night radio host floating a strange theory to night-shift listeners. Intimate, conspiratorial, curious, a little amused, leaning on 'now here is the weird part'. Around 150 to 160 words a minute.

streamer.name: Gamer streamer
streamer.style: A chill gaming streamer telling chat a wild fact mid-session. Casual, quick, genuinely hyped on the crazy bits, playful asides, laughs naturally. Around 175 to 190 words a minute.

bestie.name: Gossiping best friend
bestie.style: Your best friend spilling tea. Animated, conspiratorial, expressive reactions ('no, wait, it gets worse'), natural laughter, conversational rhythm. Around 170 to 185 words a minute.

bedtime.name: Gentle bedtime
bedtime.style: Soft, slow, soothing bedtime-story voice. Warm and gentle, rounded vowels, long calm pauses, a smile in the voice. Around 120 to 135 words a minute.

anime_premium.name: Premium anime
anime_premium.bible: High-end Japanese anime feature film look: clean confident linework, cel shading with soft gradient lighting, painterly hand-painted backgrounds with atmospheric depth, rich saturated sky gradients, lens flares and light shafts, expressive eyes, dynamic low and high angles, speed lines and impact frames on action beats, sakuga-quality motion. Characters are original designs.

anime_90s.name: 90s retro anime
anime_90s.bible: 1990s cel-animation anime on film: hand-inked lines, flat cel colours with hard shadows, film grain and slight colour bleed, painted backgrounds, VHS-era warmth, dramatic city-pop sunsets, bold silhouettes, classic mecha and cyber-city sensibility. Original characters only.

anime_shonen.name: Battle shonen
anime_shonen.bible: Explosive battle-shonen anime: thick dynamic linework, extreme foreshortening, aura glows and energy trails, debris and shockwaves, dramatic rim light, close-up eye shots before the strike, freeze-frame impact panels, heroic low-angle power poses. Original characters only.

handpainted.name: Soft hand-painted
handpainted.bible: Gentle hand-painted animation: watercolour-soft backgrounds, lush greens and warm skies, rounded friendly character shapes, gentle wind in grass and clothes, cosy everyday details, calm wonder. Original designs, no studio's characters.

cinematic_3d.name: Feature-film 3D
cinematic_3d.bible: Premium feature-animation 3D: stylised appealing characters with expressive faces, soft global illumination, subsurface skin, rich materials, shallow depth of field, warm key and cool rim light, cinematic lensing, polished like a big-studio animated film. Original designs only.

photoreal.name: Cinematic realism
photoreal.bible: Photoreal cinematic look: anamorphic 2.39 framing language inside a vertical frame, natural film lighting, practical haze, realistic materials and scale, subtle film grain, teal and amber grade, handheld or dolly camera language. Disclose as AI where it could pass for real footage.

claymation.name: Claymation
claymation.bible: Stop-motion claymation miniature set: plasticine characters with visible thumbprints, felt and card props, practical miniature lighting, shallow tilt-shift depth, slight stop-motion stepping in the motion.

paper.name: Paper diorama
paper.bible: Layered paper-cut diorama: stacked cut-paper layers with real shadows between them, visible paper texture and fibres, soft backlight glowing through thin paper, sliding parallax layers as the camera moves.

comic.name: Comic book
comic.bible: Bold comic-book panels come alive: heavy ink outlines, halftone dot shading, flat punchy colours, dramatic perspective, motion lines, on-panel sound-effect shapes without readable words.

noir.name: Film noir
noir.bible: High-contrast black and white film noir: hard key light through venetian blinds, deep shadows, rain-slick streets, cigarette-smoke haze, dutch angles, 1940s grain.

vhs.name: Found-footage VHS
vhs.bible: Found-footage VHS tape: tracking lines, chroma bleed, timestamp-less camcorder framing, low light, handheld shake, flash-lit interiors, unsettling ordinary places.

pixel.name: Pixel art
pixel.bible: Detailed 16-bit pixel art: crisp pixel clusters, limited glowing palette, parallax pixel backgrounds, sprite-style characters, retro game lighting, smooth camera pans across pixel worlds.

oil.name: Oil painting
oil.bible: Old-master oil painting brought to life: visible brushwork and impasto, chiaroscuro lighting, rich umbers and golds, allegorical staging, canvas texture, slow painterly motion.

watercolor.name: Watercolour
watercolor.bible: Loose watercolour illustration: soft washes bleeding into paper, pencil underdrawing visible, white paper glow, gentle pigment granulation, airy calm motion.

blueprint.name: Blueprint cutaway
blueprint.bible: Technical blueprint and cutaway: white linework on deep blue, exploded views, measured callout lines without readable numbers, glowing component highlights, precise orbiting camera.

explainer.name: Explainer
explainer.script: A how-does-this-actually-work or what-if explainer. Hook with a strange claim, escalate in 2 or 3 steps, twist near 40 seconds, loop line at the end.
explainer.direct: Explain through vivid physical metaphors and consequences, a clear cause-and-effect chain the eye can follow.

bizarre.name: Bizarre true story
bizarre.script: A real, strange-but-true story told like a friend who can't believe it either. Open mid-action at the weirdest moment, then rewind just enough context, build the absurd chain of events, land the 'and that's why...' payoff. Real names of places and dates where known; no invented quotes.
bizarre.direct: Shoot it like a short film with characters and locations, not an explainer: establish, complicate, absurd peak, aftermath.

apocalypse.name: Apocalypse scenario
apocalypse.script: A what-if catastrophe told as a ticking timeline (minute 1, hour 1, day 1, year 1). Grounded in real science, each step bigger, a human-scale detail at every step, an eerie or hopeful final image.
apocalypse.direct: Scale ladder: start intimate (one street, one person), widen each sequence to city, continent, planet. Light and colour degrade as it worsens. One quiet beat of silence before the final reveal.

survival.name: Survival scenario
survival.script: Second person, present tense: 'You wake up in...'. Give the viewer real survival decisions with real reasoning (rule of threes, priorities), a wrong move with consequences, a smart move that saves you, and a final line that leaves them thinking 'would I make it?'.
survival.direct: First-person and over-the-shoulder framing, tight claustrophobic shots, environmental danger as the antagonist, a ticking clock in the light (sun dropping, water rising).

timetravel.name: Time travel
timetravel.script: Drop the viewer into another era with a twist ('You time travel to 1350 with your phone...'). Show what would actually happen using real history: language, money, disease, rules, what would get you in trouble, one thing you'd be a genius for knowing. End with a sting.
timetravel.direct: Strong era contrast: period-accurate sets, costumes and light; the modern object or person is the visual anomaly in every shot.

gaming.name: Gaming lore and facts
gaming.script: A hidden fact, secret, record, cut content or real-world story behind a game or gaming culture. Open with the craziest detail, explain how it happened, land a 'devs actually...' payoff. Never claim unreleased content as fact; label rumours as rumours.
gaming.direct: Render the game-world feeling in an original style (never copy real game assets, logos, characters or UI). Use HUD-like framing and gamer camera language: third-person follow, kill-cam slow motion, map fly-overs.

hype.name: Hero hype
hype.script: Build a hero moment. Underdog setup in few words, rising stakes, a moment of doubt, then the payoff line that gives chills. Short lines, rhythm like a trailer, the biggest line arrives after a silence.
hype.direct: Build like a trailer: slow push-ins, silhouettes against light, a beat of near-silence, then the hero shot on the music drop with a low heroic angle and light burst. Speed ramps on action.

mystery.name: Unsolved mystery
mystery.script: A real unsolved or unexplained case. Cold open on the eeriest fact, lay out the clues one by one, give the best theories fairly, end on the unanswered question. Never present a theory as fact.
mystery.direct: Slow creeping camera, negative space, practical low light, evidence-board details, one jolt reveal.

silent.name: No words, just music
silent.script: No narration at all. Write 6 to 9 short on-screen text beats (2 to 7 words each) that tell the story with the pictures: setup, rising stakes, the reveal, the punchline. Each beat is a caption that sits on screen for 4 to 7 seconds.
silent.direct: Pure visual storytelling cut to music: every shot must read without words, actions are big and clear, hits on the beat, a build to one climactic image.
